MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron has almost no true positive range (max ≈0.4 vs min ≈-2.7): its weak "activations" occur on tokens that open a new clause/segment after punctuation or a formula/quote (e.g. "=", enumerator "1)", "(", ","), while it is strongly *suppressed* on common function words ("a", "the", "order", the full-width comma) near the start of a document — so it is effectively a suppression neuron for document-initial function-word positions rather than a detector of any semantic concept.

L13·N9812unmasked layer
Fires at sentence/segment boundaries (final period, ".\n") and the token right where a passage begins to repeat verbatim — i.e., it marks the seam preceding duplicated text (e.g. "GOLDEN…GOLDEN OLDIE", "The next meeting…The next meeting", "The facts don't lie…The facts don't lie"); it is strongly suppressed by mid-sentence continuation words like " games", " Again", "Along".
